_comment: Lieutenants who remember (docs/ADVENTURES.md §5.5, the nemesis rule; game/story/lieutenants.py): the villain's named hands. A trait sets how they fight (`morale`; `flee_at`, the share of their hit points where they try to get away, 0: never) and what mercy does to them (`turn`: the chance a spared one comes over to you, robbed half that; `betray`: the chance one who turned was lying). Each escape or mercy refused is a grudge (`grudge`: the most it grows; `hp` more hit points a grudge, `ac` a grudge up to `ac_max`, a better blade from `blade`); a scar from `scars` for each escape that bled them. Words: {name} the lieutenant's whole name, {short} the first name, {villain} the villain, {scar} their newest scar, {trait} and {weakness} in words. A survivor with a grudge after its villain falls is promoted (`nemesis`: the days before they come for you, the grudge they need).

weaknesses: drinks more than is good for anyone who sleeps in the open
cannot read, and hides it badly
owes money to people worse than {villain}
is afraid of fire, and keeps away from it
has a sister in a village near here who thinks they are dead
will not fight in the dark if there is any choice
talks too much when they think they have won
limps when it rains, from an old fall
prays before every fight, and takes a long time about it
looks: tall and stooped, with a long grey face
short and broad, with a shaven head and a heavy jaw
thin as a rake, all elbows and quick eyes
big, soft-spoken, with hands like shovels
wiry and weathered, with hair cut short as a soldier's
pale and neat, with a voice like a clerk's
dark-browed and handsome, and knows it
grey-bearded and hard, with the look of a hanged man reprieved
young, red-haired, with a fresh brand on one wrist
heavy and slow, with small pale eyes that miss nothing
scars: a white seam across the brow
two fingers gone from the left hand
a limp they did not have before
a raw cut from the corner of the mouth to the ear

escape: {name} has had enough. They break away and run, and they do not look back.
{name} spits blood, backs off a step, and then turns and runs for it.
"Not today," {short} says through their teeth, and goes for the edge of the fight.
{name} throws something into the fire, and in the smoke and stink they are running.
escaped: {name} got away from you. They will not forget it, or you.
{name} is gone, bleeding, into the country. Someone will tell {villain}, and {short} will tell it worse.
You lost {name} in the rough. That is not the last you will see of {short}.
{name} ran. People who run from you come back, as a rule, angrier.
returns: {name} is back, with {scar}, and this time they came ready.
It is {name} again. They have {scar} now, and a better blade, and they have been thinking about you.
"Remember me?" says {name}. You do. The {scar} is new.
{name} again, with {scar} and the look of someone who has rehearsed this.
spared_back: {name} goes back to {villain}. Mercy has only made them hate you more.
You let {name} go. They do not thank you. They go straight back to {villain}, and they will remember being on their knees.
{short} takes your mercy and runs with it, back to {villain}. Some people cannot be shamed into goodness.
turned: {name} sits a long time in the road after you let them go. Then they come after you, slowly, and tell you what they know.
"You could have cut my throat," {short} says. "{villain} would have." Then they talk, and it is worth hearing.
{name} looks at the hand you did not cut off, and then at you. "All right," they say. "Listen."
slain_grief: Somewhere, {villain} hears that {name} is dead, and for a whole night nothing else is done.
Word goes back to {villain} that {name} is dead. It is said {villain} sat with the body till dawn.
{name} is dead. People who serve {villain} say it took the news quietly, and that the quiet was worse than shouting.
slain_rage: Word goes back to {villain} that {name} is dead. Someone will pay for that, and {villain} means it to be you.
{name} is dead, and {villain} knows it before nightfall. It does not grieve. It plans.
When they bring {villain} the news of {name}, it breaks the messenger's arm. Then it asks where you are sleeping.
joins: {name} is there beside {villain}, as they always meant to be.
{name} stands at {villain}'s right hand, and grins when they see you.
And there is {name}, waiting, with their blade out.
joins_grudge: {name} is there beside {villain}, with {scar} and a grudge worth more than the blade in their hand.
{name} pushes to the front when they see you. The {scar} you gave them is still red.
"I told it you would come," says {name}, touching {scar}. "I asked for you myself."
turncoat: {name} is there beside {villain}. They were never yours. They laugh when they see your face.
And there, at {villain}'s side, is {name}, who swore to you on the road. Every word was a lie.
{name} gives you a little bow from beside {villain}. "You should have cut my throat when you could," they say.
nemesis: {name} steps out into the road ahead. {villain} is gone, and they have come to settle what is left between you.
There is a band across the road, and at its head {name}, with {scar}. "They say you killed {villain}," {short} says. "Now there is only me."
{name} has been waiting for you, a long time by the look of the camp. They have {villain}'s old company now, and one thing left to do.
"I said I would find you," says {name}, with {scar} pale in the light. The men behind them spread out.
nemesis_slain: {name} is dead at last. What was left of {villain}'s company scatters with the news.
That is the end of {name}, and of the last thing {villain} left behind.
{name} dies cursing you. Nobody comes looking for you on their account again.
nemesis_fled: {name} gets away again. You will see them on another road.
{name} is gone once more, with one more thing to hate you for.
Again {name} runs, and again they will be back.

slain: {name} lies in a shallow grave by the road, and nobody comes to stand over it.
{name} died as they lived, in {villain}'s service, and the crows had them before the week was out.
Of {name} there is only a story now, and not a kind one.
taken: {name} was given to the law, and the law was not gentle. They sit in a cell still, and talk to the wall about you.
{name} was hanged at the next assize, and said nothing on the scaffold.
{name} went in chains to the lord's justice. The last anyone heard, they were working a quarry, and older than their years.
turned: {name} kept their word to you. They have a small place now, a long way from here, and they light a candle for you on the day you spared them.
{name} went straight, as far as anyone does. When people ask about the scar, they tell your story, not theirs.
{name} was seen at a market the next spring, buying seed. They nodded to anyone who said your name.
turncoat: {name} went into the dark with {villain}'s secrets and their own. You will know better next time.
{name} lied to you and lived. Somewhere they are telling the story, and laughing at the end.
Nobody knows where {name} went after. You have a fair idea what they are doing.
free: {name} is still out there, with a grudge and a good memory.
{name} was not found among the dead. People say they went north. People say a lot of things.
{name} got clear of it all, and is somewhere now, waiting.
promoted: {name} took up what was left of {villain}'s company, and swore an oath on {scar}. They are coming for you.
With {villain} gone, {name} is the one they follow now. They have told everyone what they will do when they find you.
{name} has {villain}'s old place now, and a grudge older than the title. You will meet again.
